title: Career Roadmap — Production Coordinator
summary: A Production Coordinator manages the administrative and logistical activities required to keep a film, television programme, advertisement or digital production organised. The role connects departments, tracks schedules, coordinates resources and ensures production information reaches the right people on time.

about.label: Career domain
about.text: Film, Television, OTT, Advertising & Media Production

blocks.text: A Production Coordinator manages the administrative and logistical activities required to keep a film, television programme, advertisement or digital production organised. The role connects departments, tracks schedules, coordinates resources and ensures production information reaches the right people on time.

items.text: Coordinate shooting schedules, locations, transport and accommodation.
Prepare and distribute call sheets, contact lists and production documents.
Track equipment, props, permits and resource requirements.
Coordinate communication between cast, crew and production departments.
Monitor expenses, invoices, purchase orders and production records.
Manage schedule changes and resolve logistical problems.

blocks.text: Unlike an Assistant Director, who focuses heavily on coordinating activity on set, a Production Coordinator often concentrates on the broader administrative and logistical workflow. Responsibilities vary by production size and company.
This roadmap assumes a four-year undergraduate programme. For a three-year degree, combine the later milestones.

blocks.text: Complete these five projects during the degree.

blocks.label: Production budget
blocks.text: Prepare a sample budget for a short film, covering crew, equipment, locations, transport and contingency.

blocks.label: Production schedule
blocks.text: Create a day-by-day timeline with milestones, dependencies and resource requirements.

blocks.label: Call sheet package
blocks.text: Prepare sample call sheets and a crew contact directory.

blocks.label: Location logistics plan
blocks.text: Document location requirements, transport, permissions and contingency arrangements.

blocks.label: Production coordination case study
blocks.text: Coordinate a real or simulated short-film project and document delays, decisions and outcomes.
Clearly label simulated budgets and schedules. For real projects, include only documents you have permission to share.

A specific certification is not universally required. Practical coordination experience, accurate documentation and reliability are stronger evidence of readiness.

Production Coordinator · Senior Production Coordinator · Production Executive

Adjacent career options include Assistant Director, location coordinator, event production coordinator, project coordinator and media operations executive.
Career progression depends on production experience, budgeting capability, project complexity and the organisation's structure. These titles are not interchangeable across every industry.

A postgraduate degree is optional for many coordinator positions. Hands-on production experience and organisational skills can provide a direct entry route.
Potential destinations include the UK, USA, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. Relevant study areas include film production, production management, media operations and project management.
Before applying, verify tuition, scholarships, local hiring requirements and work authorisation. International study does not guarantee employment.

blocks.label: Primary recommendation
blocks.text: Develop strong spreadsheet, scheduling, documentation and communication skills, then apply them on student films or small productions. A portfolio of accurate production documents and evidence of successful coordination will help demonstrate job readiness.
